rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says Zechariah came during Mary's debate with the Jews and asked the infant Jesus to state his proof; Jesus was then forty days old.
rows.anchor: وهب: أتاها زكريا عند مناظرتها اليهود

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says Jesus spoke on the day he was born, rather than at forty days.
rows.anchor: مقاتل: بل هو يوم ولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus first acknowledged servitude to God so people would not take him as a deity.
rows.anchor: إني عبد الله أقر على نفسه بالعبودية لله عز وجل أول ما تكلم لئلا يتخذ إلها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The statement that Jesus received the Book and prophethood predicts that he will receive them in the future.
rows.anchor: قيل: معناه سيؤتيني الكتاب ويجعلني نبيا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the statement reports what was written for Jesus in the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هذا إخبار عما كتب له في اللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet was already a prophet while Adam was between spirit and body.
rows.anchor: للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: متى كنت نبيا؟

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most commentators say Jesus received the Gospel as a small child and had the reasoning of adult men.
rows.anchor: وقال الأكثرون أوتي الإنجيل وهو صغير طفل، وكان يعقل عقل الرجال

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says Jesus was taught the Torah while still in his mother's womb.
rows.anchor: الحسن: أنه قال: ألهم التوراة وهو في بطن أمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being blessed wherever he went means Jesus was beneficial wherever he turned.
rows.anchor: أي نفاعا حيث ما توجهت

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains Jesus's blessing as teaching people goodness.
rows.anchor: مجاهد: معلما للخير

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata says Jesus was blessed by calling people to God, His oneness, and His worship.
rows.anchor: عطاء: أدعو إلى الله وإلى توحيده وعبادته

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that Jesus was a blessing to whoever followed him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: مباركا على من تبعني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's charge to Jesus to pray and give zakat means He commanded both duties.
rows.anchor: وأوصاني بالصلاة والزكاة} أي: أمرني بهما

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: In answer to how Jesus could owe zakat without property, one view means he would pay it if he had wealth.
rows.anchor: قيل: معناه بالزكاة لو كان لي مال

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A second answer takes zakat as increasing good deeds.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بالاستكثار من الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made Jesus dutiful toward his mother and not a tyrant disobedient to his Lord.
rows.anchor: أي وجعلني برا بوالدتي، {ولم يجعلني جبارا شقيا} أي عاصيا لربه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A wretched person here is someone who sins and does not repent.
rows.anchor: قيل: "الشقي": الذي يذنب ولا يتوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Peace at birth means safety from Satan's piercing, at death from shirk, and at resurrection from terrors.
rows.anchor: أي عند الموت من الشرك، {ويوم أبعث حيا} من الأهوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus's speech made the people recognize Mary's innocence; he then remained silent until children normally begin speaking.
rows.anchor: ثم سكت عيسى عليه السلام، فلم يتكلم بعد ذلك حتى بلغ المدة التي يتكلم فيها الصبيان

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says “that” points to the one who said, “I am God's servant”: Jesus son of Mary.
rows.anchor: الزجاج: أي ذلك الذي قال إني عبد الله

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم ويعقوب
rows.claim: These readers pronounce قول الحق in the accusative as a verbal noun: Jesus spoke the true statement.
rows.anchor: ابن عامر وعاصم ويعقوب: {قول الحق} بنصب اللام وهو نصب على المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disputants differ over Jesus: some call him God's son, some God, and some a lying magician.
rows.anchor: أي: يختلفون، فقائل يقول: هو ابن الله، وقائل يقول: هو الله،

rows.speaker: الآخرون
rows.claim: The other readers put قول الحق in the nominative, meaning this speech is the true statement, as in “certainty of truth” and “true promise.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون برفع اللام، يعني: هو قول الحق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view makes the phrase an epithet of Jesus, God's true word, about whom people dispute and doubt.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو نعت لعيسى ابن مريم، يعني ذلك عيسى ابن مريم كلمة الله الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is not God's attribute to take a child; one grammatical explanation transfers the lām, meaning God would not take a child.
rows.anchor: أي: ما كان من صفته اتخاذ الولد. وقيل: اللام منقولة أي ما كان الله ليتخذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God wills to bring something into being, He only says “Be,” and it is.
rows.anchor: إذا أراد أن يحدث أمرا {فإنما يقول له كن فيكون}

rows.speaker: أهل الحجاز وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: They read أن الله with fatḥa, linking it to Jesus's statement that God commanded him to pray and give zakat, and that God is Lord of all.
rows.anchor: أهل الحجاز وأبو عمرو: {أن الله} بفتح الألف، يرجع إلى قوله

rows.speaker: أهل الشام والكوفة ويعقوب
rows.claim: They read إن الله with kasra as the beginning of a new sentence.
rows.anchor: أهل الشام والكوفة ويعقوب بكسر الألف على الاستئناف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The factions are Christians divided over Jesus into Nestorians, Melkites, and Jacobites.
rows.anchor: يعني: النصارى سموا أحزابا لأنهم تحزبوا ثلاث فرق في أمر عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threatened great day of witnessing is the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: {فويل للذين كفروا من مشهد يوم عظيم} يعني يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exclamation means the disbelievers will hear and see strikingly well at Resurrection, though hearing and sight will no longer benefit them; they perceive then what they missed in worldly life.
rows.anchor: {أسمع بهم وأبصر} أي ما أسمعهم وأبصرهم يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says no one will hear or see more acutely on Resurrection Day, when God asks Jesus, “Did you say to the people…?”
rows.anchor: الكلبي: لا أحد يوم القيامة أسمع منهم ولا أبصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers are plainly in error in the present world.
rows.anchor: {يوم يأتوننا لكن الظالمون اليوم في ضلال مبين} أي: في خطأ بين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Regret comes when judgment is finished, Paradise and Hell have received their people, and death is slaughtered.
rows.anchor: {وأنذرهم يوم الحسرة إذ قضي الأمر} فرغ من الحساب وأدخل أهل الجنة الجنة، وأهل النار النار، وذبح الموت.

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Saʿid al-Khudri reports the Prophet's account of death as a recognizable ram, slaughtered after the people identify it, followed by the announcement of everlasting life or punishment.
rows.anchor: أبي سعيد الخدري قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "يؤتى بالموت كهيئة كبش أملح

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A version reported by Abu ʿIsa adds that without God's decree of everlasting life, Paradise's joy and Hell's grief would kill their inhabitants.
rows.anchor: ورواه أبو عيسى عن أحمد بن منيع، عن النضر بن إسماعيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people are heedless of what will be done to them in the afterlife and do not believe it.
rows.anchor: {وهم في غفلة} أي: عما يفعل بهم في الآخرة {وهم لا يؤمنون} لا يصدقون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God inherits the earth by causing its inhabitants all to die, leaving the Lord alone; people return to Him for recompense according to their deeds.
rows.anchor: {إنا نحن نرث الأرض ومن عليها} أي: نميت سكان الأرض ونهلكهم جميعا، ويبقى الرب وحده فيرثهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ṣiddīq is one abundant in truth and steadfast in it.
rows.anchor: الصديق": الكثير الصدق القائم عليه. وقيل:

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another definition makes a ṣiddīq one who affirms God's oneness, His messengers, and resurrection, and acts on God's commands.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من صدق الله في وحدانيته وصدق أنبياءه ورسله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophet is elevated in rank because God sent him.
rows.anchor: النبي": العالي في الرتبة بإرسال الله تعالى إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's father is identified as Azar, who worshipped idols.
rows.anchor: {إذ قال} إبراهيم {لأبيه} آزر وهو يعبد الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham says idols cannot hear sounds, see anything, or provide any benefit or sufficiency.
rows.anchor: {يا أبت لم تعبد ما لا يسمع} صوتا {ولا يبصر} شيئا {ولا يغني عنك} أي لا يكفيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The knowledge that came to Abraham is knowledge of God and spiritual recognition; following him leads to a straight path.
rows.anchor: {يا أبت إني قد جاءني من العلم} بالله والمعرفة {ما لم يأتك فاتبعني} على ديني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worshipping Satan means obeying his embellishments of disbelief and shirk; “was” describes Satan's present state.
rows.anchor: لا تطعه فيما يزين لك من الكفر والشرك {إن الشيطان كان للرحمن عصيا} عاصيا "كان" بمعنى الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's “I fear” means “I know”; the punishment touches his father if he persists in disbelief, making him Satan's companion in Hell.
rows.anchor: أي: إن أقمت على الكفر {فتكون للشيطان وليا} قرينا في النار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's father asks whether Abraham is turning away from his idols.
rows.anchor: {قال} أبوه مجيبا له: {أراغب أنت عن آلهتي يا إبراهيم

rows.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل والضحاك
rows.claim: They interpret the threat to stone Abraham as insulting him with vile speech and driving him away through abusive words.
rows.anchor: الكلبي ومقاتل والضحاك: لأشتمنك ولأبعدنك عني بالقول القبيح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas interprets the threat as beating Abraham.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس لأضربنك.

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima interprets the threat as killing Abraham with stones.
rows.anchor: عكرمة: لأقتلنك بالحجارة.

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says “for a long while” means stay far away from me for a long time.
rows.anchor: الكلبي: اجنبني طويلا.

rows.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة
rows.claim: Mujahid and ʿIkrima take the phrase to mean for a time.
rows.anchor: مجاهد وعكرمة: حينا.

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says it means for an age; the root sense of ḥīn is remaining.
rows.anchor: سعيد بن جبير: دهرا وأصل "الحين": المكث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dual al-malawān is a name for night and day.
rows.anchor: "والملوان": الليل والنهار

rows.speaker: قتادة وعطاء
rows.claim: Qatada and Ata explain the phrase as “safely.”
rows.anchor: قتادة وعطاء: سالما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Abraham is to leave safely, without his father inflicting harm; a person “mali” in a matter is capable of it.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: اعتزلني سالما لا تصيبك مني معرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham promises peace meaning he will do his father no harm, since he was not commanded to fight him for disbelief.
rows.anchor: {قال} إبراهيم {سلام عليك} أي سلمت مني لا أصيبك بمكروه، وذلك أنه لم يؤمر بقتاله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view understands this as a farewell and separation greeting.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هذا سلام هجران ومفارقة.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view takes it as gentle filial kindness, the wise person's reply to a fool, and links it to 25:63.
rows.anchor: وقيل: سلام بر ولطف وهو جواب الحليم للسفيه. قال الله تعالى:

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation says that, having exhausted his efforts, Abraham promised to ask God to guide his father to monotheism and forgive him.
rows.anchor: قيل: إنه لما أعياه أمره ووعده أن يراجع الله فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking forgiveness means asking God to grant his father repentance through which he could receive forgiveness.
rows.anchor: معناه: سأسأل الله تعالى لك توبة تنال بها المغفرة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being gracious to Abraham means being kind and gentle toward him.
rows.anchor: {إنه كان بي حفيا} برا لطيفا.

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says God knew Abraham and answered him when he prayed.
rows.anchor: الكلبي: عالما يستجيب لي إذا دعوته.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says God had made Abraham accustomed to answered prayers.
rows.anchor: مجاهد: عودني الإجابة لدعائي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's separation from his people includes separation from what they worship besides God.
rows.anchor: {وأعتزلكم وما تدعون من دون الله} أي: أعتزل ما تعبدون

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says Abraham left his people at Kutha and emigrated to the Holy Land.
rows.anchor: مقاتل: كان اعتزاله إياهم أنه فارقهم من "كوثى"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling on Abraham's Lord means worshipping Him and hoping not to be wretched as the idolaters are through their worship.
rows.anchor: {وأدعو ربي} أي: أعبد ربي {عسى ألا أكون بدعاء ربي شقيا}

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation hopes God will answer Abraham when called and not disappoint him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: عسى أن يجيبني إذا دعوته ولا يخيبني.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Abraham emigrated away from them and their gods, God gave him Isaac and Jacob, easing his loneliness and comforting him with children dear to God.
rows.anchor: {وهبنا له} بعد الهجرة {إسحاق ويعقوب} آنسنا وحشته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both Isaac and Jacob were made prophets.
rows.anchor: {وكلا جعلنا نبيا} يعني: إسحاق ويعقوب.

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi and most commentators understand God's mercy to Abraham and his descendants as wealth and children, the worldly abundance of provision.
rows.anchor: الكلبي: المال والولد، وهو قول الأكثرين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies the gift of mercy as scripture and prophethood.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الكتاب والنبوة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A lofty “tongue of truth” is an excellent and elevated reputation among all religious communities, who honor and praise them.
rows.anchor: يعني ثناء حسنا رفيعا في كل أهل الأديان، فكلهم يتولونهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses was sincerely devoted, without dissimulation, in worship and obedience to God.
rows.anchor: {واذكر في الكتاب موسى إنه كان مخلصا} غير مراء أخلص العبادة والطاعة لله عز وجل

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة
rows.claim: Kufa's reading with a fatḥa on the lām means chosen by God.
rows.anchor: أهل الكوفة " مخلصا " بفتح اللام أي: مختارا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says God selected Moses and purified him from defilement.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أخلصه الله من الدنس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The right side of the mountain is the side to Moses's right; the mountain lies between Egypt and Midian and is also called al-Zubayr.
rows.anchor: {وناديناه من جانب الطور الأيمن} يعني: يمين موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This occurred when Moses came from Midian, saw the fire, and was called by God, “I am Allah, Lord of the worlds.”
rows.anchor: وذلك حين أقبل من مدين ورأى النار فنودي "يا موسى إني أنا الله رب العالمين"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A najī is someone spoken to privately, like a companion or close friend.
rows.anchor: {وقربناه نجيا} أي" مناجيا، فالنجي المناجي، كما يقال: جليس ونديم.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says God brought Moses near and spoke to him; nearness means making him hear God's speech.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: معناه: قربه فكلمه، ومعنى التقريب:

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report says Moses was raised beyond the veils until he heard the pen's scratching.
rows.anchor: وقيل: رفعه على الحجب حتى سمع صرير القلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave Moses Aaron in answer to Moses's prayer for Aaron to be his minister; this is why Aaron is called a gift.
rows.anchor: موسى فقال: "واجعل لي وزيرا من أهلي هارون أخي"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This Ishmael is Abraham's son and the ancestor of the Prophet Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وهو إسماعيل بن إبراهيم جد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says Ishmael never made a promise without fulfilling it.
rows.anchor: مجاهد: لم يعد شيئا إلا وفى به.

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says Ishmael promised a man to stay in his place until he returned, and waited there three days.
rows.anchor: مقاتل: وعد رجلا أن يقيم مكانه حتى يرجع إليه الرجل، فأقام إسماعيل مكانه ثلاثة أيام

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says Ishmael waited for the man until a full year had passed.
rows.anchor: الكلبي: انتظره حتى حال عليه الحول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishmael was a messenger to Jurhum and a prophet who conveyed reports from God.
rows.anchor: {وكان رسولا} إلى جرهم {نبيا} مخبرا عن الله عز وجل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “His family” means his people; another view extends it to his family and all his community.
rows.anchor: أهله} أي: قومه وقيل: أهله وجميع أمته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the prayer and zakat are the duties God prescribed to them, the ḥanīfiyya also prescribed to Muslims.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: يريد التي افترضها الله تعالى عليهم، وهي الحنيفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishmael pleased God by maintaining obedience.
rows.anchor: {وكان عند ربه مرضيا} قائما بطاعته.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says God approved Ishmael for prophethood and messengership.
rows.anchor: قيل: رضيه الله عز وجل لنبوته ورسالته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idris was Noah's grandfather, named Akhnukh; he was called Idris because he studied scriptures extensively.
rows.anchor: وهو جد أبي نوح واسمه "أخنوخ" سمي إدريس لكثرة درسه الكتب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idris was a tailor, first to write with a pen and sew and wear sewn clothing; he also first made weapons, fought disbelievers, and studied astronomy and arithmetic.
rows.anchor: وكان خياطا وهو أول من خط بالقلم، وأول من خاط الثياب، ولبس المخيط

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says Idris was raised to Paradise.
rows.anchor: قيل: يعني الجنة.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes the raising as worldly elevation of rank.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي الرفعة بعلو الرتبة في الدنيا.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third view says Idris was raised to the fourth heaven.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو أنه رفع إلى السماء الرابعة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Anas ibn Malik, from Malik ibn Saʿsaʿa, reports that the Prophet saw Idris in the fourth heaven during the Night Journey.
rows.anchor: أنس بن مالك عن مالك بن صعصعة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه رأى إدريس

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb and others say Idris asked God to lighten the sun's burden and heat for its angel; the angel then visited Idris, sought a delay of his death, and the story ends with Idris dying where the sun rises.
rows.anchor: على ما قاله كعب وغيره: أنه سار ذات يوم في حاجة فأصابه وهج الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars disagree whether Idris is alive in heaven or dead; those who say he lives count Idris and Jesus in heaven and Khidr and Ilyas on earth among four living prophets.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا في أنه حي في السماء أم ميت؟ فقال قوم: هو ميت وقال قوم: هو حي

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb relates that Idris's extraordinary worship drew the angels' wonder and the Angel of Death's longing; after visiting, the Angel of Death granted Idris's request to experience death, restored him, and took him to see Heaven and Hell.
rows.anchor: وهب: كان يرفع لإدريس كل يوم من العبادة مثل ما يرفع لجميع أهل الأرض

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: In Wahb's account, Idris argues that he has tasted death and entered Hell, then asks to stay in Paradise; God confirms he entered by permission and will remain alive there.
rows.anchor: قال: "كل نفس ذائقة الموت" (آل عمران:185) وقد ذقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wicked generation succeeded the prophets; the source distinguishes khalaf with fatḥa as righteous and with sukūn as wicked.
rows.anchor: من بعد النبيين المذكورين خلف وهم قوم سوء، "والخلف" -بالفتح-الصالح، وبالجزم الطالح

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the generation as Jews and those who joined them.
rows.anchor: السدي: أراد بهم اليهود ومن لحق بهم.

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Mujahid and Qatada say the passage refers to people in this Muslim community.
rows.anchor: مجاهد وقتادة: هم في هذه الأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Squandering prayer means abandoning the obligatory prayers.
rows.anchor: {أضاعوا الصلاة} تركوا الصلاة المفروضة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وإبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud and Ibrahim say it means delaying prayer beyond its proper time.
rows.anchor: ابن مسعود وإبراهيم: أخروها عن وقتها.

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib specifies delaying noon prayer until afternoon and afternoon prayer until sunset.
rows.anchor: سعيد بن المسيب: هو أن لا يصلي الظهر حتى يأتي العصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following desires means preferring sins and wine over obedience.
rows.anchor: {واتبعوا الشهوات} أي المعاصي وشرب الخمر، يعني آثروا شهوات أنفسهم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid describes a late-age group having sex with one another in markets and alleys.
rows.anchor: مجاهد: هؤلاء قوم يظهرون في آخر الزمان ينزو بعضهم على بعض

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says ghayy is a river in Hell, deep at its bottom and foul in taste.
rows.anchor: وهب: "الغي" نهر في جهنم بعيد قعره خبيث طعمه.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says ghayy is a valley whose heat Hell's valleys seek refuge from, prepared for persistent adulterers, habitual drinkers, unrepentant usurers, the undutiful, and false witnesses.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: "الغي" واد في جهنم

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata describes ghayy as a valley in Hell that flows with pus and blood.
rows.anchor: عطاء: "الغي": واد في جهنم يسيل قيحا ودما.

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb says ghayy is Hell's deepest and hottest valley in a pit called al-Him, which God opens to rekindle Hell whenever it subsides.
rows.anchor: كعب: هو واد في جهنم أبعدها قعرا، وأشدها حرا في بئر تسمى "الهيم"

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة الباهلي
rows.claim: Abu Umama reports that the distance from Hell's rim to its bottom is seventy autumns for a falling stone; below is ghayy and athām.
rows.anchor: أبا أمامة الباهلي يقول: "إن ما بين شفير جهنم إلى قعرها مسيرة سبعين خريفا

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة الباهلي
rows.claim: The report concludes that beneath the stone's destination are ghayy and athām.
rows.anchor: قال: نعم غي وآثام"

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak explains ghayy as loss; other explanations call it destruction or punishment.
rows.anchor: الضحاك: غيا وخسرانا. وقيل: هلاكا. وقيل: عذابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means more than merely seeing ghayy: it means meeting and being involved with it as well as seeing it.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {فسوف يلقون غيا} ليس معناه يرون فقط، بل معناه الاجتماع والملابسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessed servants had not seen the Gardens of Eden when they were promised them.
rows.anchor: {جنات عدن التي وعد الرحمن عباده بالغيب} ولم يروها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive participle مأتيا functions as an active one, meaning “coming.”
rows.anchor: {إنه كان وعده مأتيا} يعني: آتيا مفعول بمعنى فاعل.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Arabic allows both “fifty years came upon me” and “I came upon fifty years,” as it does “good reached me” and “I reached good.”
rows.anchor: وقيل: لم يقل آتيا لأن كل من أتاك فقد أتيته والعرب لا تفرق

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir takes “His promise” as the appointed meeting, Paradise, which God's friends and obedient servants will reach.
rows.anchor: ابن جرير: "وعده" أي: موعده وهو الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laghw in Paradise means falsehood, obscenity, and pointless excess in speech.
rows.anchor: في الجنة {لغوا} باطلا وفحشا وفضولا من الكلام

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil identifies the pointless speech as a false oath.
rows.anchor: مقاتل: هو اليمين الكاذبة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is of a different kind: Paradise's people hear greetings, a comprehensive good that includes safety, rather than anything sinful.
rows.anchor: استثناء من غير جنسه يعني: بل يسمعون فيها سلاما أي: قولا يسلمون منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salām is a comprehensive name for good because it includes safety; the people hear what does not make them sin.
rows.anchor: اسم جامع للخير لأنه يتضمن السلامة.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says Paradise's people greet one another and are greeted by angels.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو تسليم بعضهم على بعض وتسليم الملائكة عليهم.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says God greets the people of Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو تسليم الله عليهم.

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Although Paradise has perpetual light and no recognizable night, its food comes at times corresponding to the two ends of the day.
rows.anchor: أهل التفسير: ليس في الجنة ليل يعرف به البكرة والعشي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says people recognize daytime when curtains rise and night when they fall.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنهم يعرفون وقت النهار برفع الحجب ووقت الليل بإرخاء الحجب.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation treats morning and evening as an image of ease and abundant provision without restriction.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المراد منه رفاهية العيش وسعة الرزق من غير تضييق.

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says Arabs considered morning and evening food the best life, so God describes Paradise with it.
rows.anchor: الحسن البصري يقول: كانت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives and assigns Paradise to His servants.
rows.anchor: {تلك الجنة التي نورث من عبادنا} أي: نعطي وننزل.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says believers inherit the dwellings that would have belonged to Hell's people had they believed.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يورث عباده المؤمنين المساكن التي كانت لأهل النار

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that the Prophet asked Gabriel why he did not visit, and the verse came as the answer.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "يا جبريل ما يمنعك أن تزورنا"

rows.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك وقتادة ومقاتل والكلبي
rows.claim: They say Gabriel delayed after the Prophet promised answers about the Cave, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the Spirit without saying “if God wills”; Gabriel explained he was a commanded servant, and God also sent 93:1–3.
rows.anchor: عكرمة والضحاك وقتادة ومقاتل والكلبي: احتبس جبريل عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وقتادة ومقاتل
rows.claim: They say “before us” refers to afterlife, reward, and punishment; “behind us” to past worldly life; and “between” to now through Resurrection.
rows.anchor: سعيد بن جبير وقتادة ومقاتل: {ما بين أيدينا} من أمر الآخرة والثواب والعقاب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes “before us” the remaining world, “behind us” what has passed, and “between” the forty years between the two trumpet blasts.
rows.anchor: وقيل {ما بين أيدينا} ما بقي من الدنيا {وما خلفنا} ما مضى منها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says “between” is the span of our lives, with before and behind still meaning future and past worldly life.
rows.anchor: وقيل: {ما بين أيدينا} ما بقي من الدنيا {وما خلفنا} ما مضى منها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes “before us” as after death, “behind us” as before creation, and “between” as the life span.
rows.anchor: وقيل: {ما بين أيدينا} بعد أن نموت {وما خلفنا} قبل أن نخلق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says before us is the earth to which angels descend, behind us is the heaven from which they descend, and between is the air; all belong to God and angels act only by His command.
rows.anchor: وقيل: {ما بين أيدينا} الأرض إذا أردنا النزول إليها {وما خلفنا} السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is not forgetful: He has not forgotten or abandoned the Prophet.
rows.anchor: {وما كان ربك نسيا} أي: ناسيا يقول: ما نسيك ربك أي: ما تركك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship God and persevere in worship by patiently observing His commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: فاعبده واصطبر لعبادته} أي: اصبر على أمره ونهيه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas interprets “namesake” as an equal or counterpart to God.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: مثلا

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi asks whether anyone besides God is called Allah.
rows.anchor: الكلبي: هل تعلم أحدا يسمى "الله" غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person denying resurrection is Ubayy ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi, who mocks and rejects the prospect of being raised alive after death.
rows.anchor: يعني: أبي بن خلف الجمحي كان منكرا للبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says it mockingly and to deny resurrection.
rows.anchor: قاله استهزاء وتكذيبا للبعث.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Does he not remember?” means consider and reflect: the denier should infer resurrection from his own creation when he was nothing.
rows.anchor: أولا يذكر} أي يتذكر ويتفكر

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وعاصم ويعقوب
rows.claim: These readers recite يذكر with a light consonant.
rows.anchor: نافع وابن عامر وعاصم ويعقوب " يذكر " خفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God swears to gather the disbelievers who deny resurrection with the devils; each unbeliever is chained to his own devil.
rows.anchor: {فوربك لنحشرنهم} لنجمعنهم في المعاد يعني: المشركين المنكرين للبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are gathered with their satans in chains around or in Hell.
rows.anchor: يحشر كل كافر مع شيطانه في سلسلة {ثم لنحضرنهم حول جهنم} قيل في جهنم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says juthiyyan means groups gathered together.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس رضي الله عنه: جماعات جمع جثوة.

rows.speaker: الحسن والضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and al-Dahhak derive the word from jathin, meaning crouched on their knees.
rows.anchor: الحسن والضحاك: جمع "جاث" أي: جاثين على الركب.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says they stand on their knees because the place is cramped.
rows.anchor: السدي: قائمين على الركب لضيق المكان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To extract from every faction means to bring out of every unbelieving community and religious group.
rows.anchor: {من كل شيعة} أي: من كل أمة وأهل دين من الكفار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains insolence as boldness.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: يعني جرأة.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains insolence as wickedness, with the most rebellious brought out first.
rows.anchor: مجاهد: فجورا، يريد: الأعتى فالأعتى.

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the phrase means each faction's leader and chief in evil, so the greatest criminals are brought forward first.
rows.anchor: الكلبي: قائدهم ورأسهم في الشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says people are chained around Hell and the most unbelieving are brought forward first.
rows.anchor: في بعض الآثار: أنهم يحشرون جميعا حول جهنم مسلسلين مغلولين ثم يقدم الأكفر فالأكفر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative أيهم means “those of whom it is said: which are most insolent”; another analysis treats it as a new sentence, with the verb governing من كل شيعة.
rows.anchor: ورفع {أيهم} على معنى: الذي يقال لهم: أيهم أشد على الرحمن عتيا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those most deserving of burning are the ones most entitled to enter Hell and endure its heat; ṣaliya is explained with verbal forms for entering and suffering it.
rows.anchor: أي: أحق بدخول النار يقال: صلي يصلى صليا، مثل: لقي يلقى لقيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can be expanded as “there is none among you except that he will arrive at it”; warūd means reaching a place, and an oath may be implicit.
rows.anchor: وإن منكم إلا واردها} وما منكم إلا واردها وقيل: القسم فيه مضمر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, with the majority, says warūd means entering Hell, and the pronoun refers to Hell; both righteous and wicked enter, then God saves the pious.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما وهو قول الأكثرين؛ معنى الورود هاهنا هو الدخول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evidence that warūd means entering is Pharaoh's people being led by their leader into the Fire.
rows.anchor: قول الله عز وجل حكاية عن فرعون: "يقدم قومه يوم القيامة فأوردهم النار"

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: When Nafiʿ ibn al-Azraq disputed this with Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn ʿAbbas cited 21:98 to prove entry, said both would enter, and hoped God would rescue him but rejected Nafiʿ's denial.
rows.anchor: أن نافع بن الأزرق مارى ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في الورود فقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: هو الدخول.

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Others say believers never enter Hell, citing 21:101–102; all who enter remain there, so warūd means coming into view, as at Midian's water.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: ليس المراد من الورود الدخول، وقالوا النار لا يدخلها مؤمن أبدا

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima says the verse concerns disbelievers, who enter Hell and do not leave it.
rows.anchor: عكرمة: الآية في الكفار فإنهم يدخلونها ولا يخرجون منها

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Masʿud says “arriving at it” means Resurrection, and the pronoun refers to Resurrection.
rows.anchor: ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه أنه قال: {وإن منكم إلا واردها} يعني: القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Baghawi says the first interpretation is sounder and is Sunni teaching: everyone enters Hell, then God rescues believers, as the next verse shows.
rows.anchor: والأول أصح وعليه أهل السنة أنهم جميعا يدخلون النار ثم يخرج الله عز وجل منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those rescued are believers who avoided shirk; rescue implies that they had entered what they are rescued from.
rows.anchor: أي اتقوا الشرك وهم المؤمنون. والنجاة إنما تكون مما دخلت فيه

rows.speaker: الكسائي ويعقوب
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi and Yaʿqub read ننجي with a light consonant; the other readers use the doubled consonant.
rows.anchor: الكسائي ويعقوب: " ننجي " بالتخفيف. والآخرون: بالتشديد.

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that a Muslim whose three children die will not enter the Fire except as a brief fulfillment of the oath, which al-Baghawi identifies as 19:71.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم "لا يموت لمسلم ثلاثة من الولد

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Anas reports that anyone with even a barley grain, wheat grain, or atom's weight of good—or, in Aban's version, faith—is brought out of the Fire.
rows.anchor: عن أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "يخرج من النار من قال لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu al-Zilal reports from Anas a story of a man who called on God for a thousand years in Hell; God ordered Gabriel to retrieve him, then left him out after he feared being returned.
rows.anchor: أبو الظلال عن أنس بن مالك عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "أن رجلا في النار ينادي ألف سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone's arrival in Hell was an unavoidable decree; God rescues the pious and leaves the wrongdoers, the polytheists, crouched there. This proves all entered and the believers were rescued.
rows.anchor: كان ورودكم جهنم حتما لازما {مقضيا} قضاه الله عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi reads ننجي with a light consonant and the other readers double it; the crouched wrongdoers are polytheists.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي " ننجي " بالتخفيف والباقون بالتشديد {ونذر الظالمين فيها جثيا} جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A long report from Abu Hurayra compares seeing God to seeing the full moon or sun, then describes people following what they worship, the Bridge, hooks, and believers rescued by prostration marks and restored by the water of life.
rows.anchor: أن أبا هريرة أخبرهما أن الناس قالوا: يا رسول الله هل نرى ربنا يوم القيامة؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same report describes the last person leaving Hell and entering Paradise after repeatedly asking God to move him farther from the Fire and finally admit him.
rows.anchor: ويبقى رجل بين الجنة والنار وهو آخر أهل النار دخولا الجنة مقبل بوجهه قبل النار

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Hafsa reports the Prophet hoping, God willing, that no participant at Badr and al-Hudaybiyya enters Hell; when she cites 19:71, he answers by citing the rescue of the pious in 19:72.
rows.anchor: عن حفصة أنها قالت: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إني لأرجو أن لا يدخل النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers are al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and other Quraysh; believers are the Prophet's poor companions, whose rough living and clothes contrasted with idolaters' groomed hair, oil, and silk.
rows.anchor: يعني: النضر بن الحارث وذويه من قريش {للذين آمنوا} يعني فقراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maqām means residence and dwelling; Ibn Kathir's reading with ḍamma means staying or residence.
rows.anchor: مقاما} منزلا ومسكنا [وهو موضع الإقامة.

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reads مقاما with ḍamma on the mīm, meaning residence.
rows.anchor: ابن كثير: " مقاما " بضم الميم أي إقامة]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nadi means an assembly or gathering place.
rows.anchor: {وأحسن نديا} أي مجلسا ومثله النادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answers their boast by recalling past generations who were destroyed despite having better furnishings, possessions, and wealth.
rows.anchor: {وكم أهلكنا قبلهم من قرن هم أحسن أثاثا} أي متاعا وأموالا.

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil explains the generations' superior furnishings as better clothes.
rows.anchor: مقاتل: لباسا وثيابا

rows.speaker: أكثر القراء
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce رئيا with hamza, meaning appearance or what is seen.
rows.anchor: أكثر القراء بالهمز أي: منظرا من "الرؤية"

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو جعفر ونافع غير ورش
rows.claim: These readers pronounce it riyyā without hamza: either the same word with hamza removed or luxuriant prosperity that appears in one's looks.
rows.anchor: ابن عامر وأبو جعفر ونافع غير ورش: "وريا" مشددا بغير همز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command that God let the astray continue is declarative in meaning: He leaves them in transgression and grants respite in disbelief.
rows.anchor: هذا أمر بمعنى الخبر معناه: يدعه في طغيانه ويمهله في كفره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised punishment may be captivity and killing in this world, or Resurrection, when they enter Hell.
rows.anchor: إما العذاب} وهو الأسر والقتل في الدنيا {وإما الساعة} يعني: القيامة فيدخلون النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will learn who has the worse place and weaker support: unbelievers are in Hell while believers are in Paradise, rebutting their earlier boast.
rows.anchor: وهذا رد عليهم في قوله {أي الفريقين خير مقاما وأحسن نديا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God increases the guided in guidance by adding faith and certainty to their certainty.
rows.anchor: {ويزيد الله الذين اهتدوا هدى} أي إيمانا وإيقانا على يقينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lasting good things are enduring acts of worship and righteous deeds; they are better in reward and final return.
rows.anchor: والباقيات الصالحات} الأذكار والأعمال الصالحة التي تبقى لصاحبها

rows.speaker: خباب
rows.claim: Khabbab says al-ʿAs ibn Waʾil owed him wages for metalwork but refused to pay until Khabbab renounced Muhammad; al-ʿAs claimed that after resurrection he would have wealth and children to repay him, prompting this verse.
rows.anchor: خباب قال: كنت قينا فعملت للعاص بن وائل فاجتمع مالي عنده

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas asks whether the man has looked into the Preserved Tablet to know the unseen.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: أنظر في اللوح المحفوظ؟

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid asks whether the man knows the unseen well enough to know if he is destined for Paradise.
rows.anchor: مجاهد: أعلم علم الغيب حتى يعلم أفي الجنة هو أم لا؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having a covenant with the Merciful means saying “There is no god but God.”
rows.anchor: يعني قال لا إله إلا الله وقال قتادة:

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the covenant is a righteous deed sent ahead.
rows.anchor: قتادة: يعني عملا صالحا قدمه.

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi takes the question to mean: did God promise him that he would enter Paradise?
rows.anchor: الكلبي: أعهد إليه أن يدخل الجنة؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuttal denies the man's claim; God will preserve it and requite him, either by ordering angels to write his words or simply keeping them on record.
rows.anchor: {كلا} رد عليه يعني: لم يفعل ذلك {سنكتب} سنحفظ عليه {ما يقول}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Increasing punishment means either adding punishment beyond his existing punishment or prolonging its duration.
rows.anchor: أي: نزيده عذابا فوق العذاب. وقيل: نطيل مدة عذابه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God inherits the wealth and children the man claimed by destroying him and nullifying his dominion; the inheritance concerns possessions beneath his claim to have them in the next life.
rows.anchor: ونرثه ما يقول} أي ما عنده من المال والولد بإهلاكنا إياه وإبطال ملكه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation says God preserves what the man says so He can requite him for it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معنى قوله: {ونرثه ما يقول} أي: نحفظ ما يقول حتى نجازيه به.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He comes to God on Resurrection Day alone, without wealth or children.
rows.anchor: ويأتينا فردا} يوم القيامة بلا مال ولا ولد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh idolaters took idols as gods to provide protection and intercession, shielding them from punishment.
rows.anchor: يعني: مشركي قريش اتخذوا الأصنام آلهة يعبدونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols will repudiate their worshippers and deny that the latter worshipped them, as in 28:63.
rows.anchor: كما أخبر الله تعالى "تبرأنا إليك ما كانوا إيانا يعبدون"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols will become enemies of people who treated them as allies in worldly life.
rows.anchor: أي أعداء لهم وكانوا أولياءهم في الدنيا.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes the idols as helpers against their worshippers, calling them liars and cursing them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أعوانا عليهم يكذبونهم ويلعنونهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God empowered devils over disbelievers, as when He told Iblis to incite whomever he could in 17:64.
rows.anchor: أي سلطناهم عليهم وذلك حين قال لإبليس: "واستفزز من استطعت منهم بصوتك"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The devils' urging is agitation from obedience toward disobedience; the word azz means to move or stir, as does hazz.
rows.anchor: تزعجهم إزعاجا من الطاعة إلى المعصية "والأز" "والهز": التحريك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command not to hurry is not to hasten the demand that the disbelievers be punished.
rows.anchor: فلا تعجل عليهم} أي لا تعجل بطلب عقوبتهم

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says God counts the nights, days, months, and years of their term.
rows.anchor: الكلبي: يعني الليالي والأيام والشهور والأعوام.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation counts the breaths they take until the appointed term of their punishment.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الأنفاس التي يتنفسون بها في الدنيا إلى الأجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to recall the day when the God-fearing, obedient people are gathered as a delegation to the Merciful and to Paradise.
rows.anchor: أي: اذكر لهم يا محمد اليوم الذي يجمع فيه من اتقى الله في الدنيا بطاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wafd means groups of emissaries and is the plural of wāfid, like rider/party and companion/companions.
rows.anchor: وفدا أي: جماعات جمع "وافد" مثل: راكب وركب وصاحب وصحب.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the delegates ride camels.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: ركبانا.

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra says they ride camels.
rows.anchor: أبو هريرة: على الإبل.

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: ʿAli says they ride she-camels with golden saddles and jeweled mounts that travel on foot or fly as their riders wish.
rows.anchor: علي بن أبي طالب: ما يحشرون والله على أرجلهم، ولكن على نوق رحالها الذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals are disbelievers driven to Hell on foot, or thirsty; a group approaching water is called wird because they come only after thirst.
rows.anchor: ونسوق المجرمين} الكافرين {إلى جهنم وردا} أي مشاة. وقيل: عطاشا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant granting intercession means affirming that there is no god but God.
rows.anchor: يعني لا إله إلا الله.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says intercessors may intercede only for someone with a covenant—that is, believers—as in 21:28.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه لا يشفع الشافعون إلا لمن اتخذ عند الرحمن عهدا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says only one who testifies that there is no god but God, a believer, may intercede.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لا يشفع إلا من شهد أن لا إله إلا الله أي لا يشفع إلا المؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who claim God has a child include Jews, Christians, and anyone who says the angels are God's daughters.
rows.anchor: يعني اليهود والنصارى ومن زعم أن الملائكة بنات الله.

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read walad with ḍamma on wāw and sukūn on lām here, in al-Zukhruf, and in Surah Nuh.
rows.anchor: حمزة والكسائي " ولدا " بضم الواو وسكون اللام

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ويعقوب
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʿAmr, and Yaʿqub agree with that reading in Surah Nuh; others use fatḥa on both letters, and both forms are dialect variants.
rows.anchor: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ويعقوب في سورة نوح والباقون بفتح الواو واللام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the claim is reprehensible.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس منكرا.

rows.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
rows.claim: Qatada and Mujahid explain iddan as something immense.
rows.anchor: قتادة ومجاهد: عظيما.

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil paraphrases the claim as an enormously grave statement.
rows.anchor: مقاتل: لقد قلتم قولا عظيما.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, idd denotes the greatest calamities.
rows.anchor: والإد" في كلام العرب: أعظم الدواهي

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nafiʿ reads يكاد with yāʾ because it precedes the verb; the others use feminine تكاد because “heavens” is feminine.
rows.anchor: نافع " يكاد " بالياء هاهنا وفي حم عسق لتقدم الفعل

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وأبو بكر ويعقوب
rows.claim: They read يتفطرن with nūn from انفطار here and in 42:5; Ibn ʿAmir and Hamza agree here, matching 82:1 and 73:18.
rows.anchor: أبو عمرو وأبو بكر ويعقوب وافق ابن عامر وحمزة هاهنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readers use tāʾ from تفطر; انفطر and تفطر both mean to split or crack.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالتاء من التفطر ومعناهما واحد يقال: انفطر الشيء وتفطر أي تشقق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains collapse in pieces; earth's splitting may mean it caves in on the claimants, sky's splitting means falling upon them, and the mountains crush them as they collapse.
rows.anchor: {وتنشق الأرض} أي: تنخسف بهم "والانفطار" في السماء: أن تسقط عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the Qur'an easy in Muhammad's language so he could give good news to believers who fear God and warn combative opponents.
rows.anchor: أي سهلنا القرآن بلسانك يا محمد {لتبشر به المتقين} يعني المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ludd is the plural of al-ald and describes people who are severe in argument.
rows.anchor: شدادا في الخصومة جمع "الألد".

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says ludd means deaf to the truth.
rows.anchor: الحسن: صما عن الحق

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid defines an ald as an unjust person who does not act rightly.
rows.anchor: مجاهد: 10/ب "الألد": الظالم الذي لا يستقيم

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu ʿUbayda says an ald refuses truth and asserts falsehood.
rows.anchor: أبو عبيدة: "الألد" الذي لا يقبل الحق ويدعي الباطل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To sense a person means to see or find one; rakz is a faint sound.
rows.anchor: هل تحس} هل ترى وقيل هل تجد {منهم من أحد أو تسمع لهم ركزا} أي صوتا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the earlier generations all perished, leaving no trace or evidence.
rows.anchor: الحسن: بادوا جميعا فلم يبق منهم عين ولا أثر
